title: Fig and almond cake
subtitle: a moist almond sponge with fresh figs pressed into the batter before baking
excerpt: Fig and almond cake is a moist, fragrant sponge made mostly from ground almonds with fresh figs halved and pressed into the batter so they sink slightly and caramelise around the edges during baking. The almond base is dense and a little honey-sweet. It is better the day after baking when the fig juices have soaked into the crumb.
sourceNotes: Almond cake with fresh fruit baked in is documented in Italian and Middle Eastern baking traditions. The combination of figs and almonds is common in Mediterranean cookery.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before. Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 days.

content.text: Fig and almond cake is a flourless almond sponge with ripe figs pressed in before baking. The figs sink slightly as the cake bakes and caramelise in the heat, giving jammy pockets through the dense, honey-sweetened crumb. The cake is best left to cool completely and then left overnight before slicing.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease a 23 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, and honey together until smooth. Fold in the ground almonds, baking powder, and almond extract if using.
Pour the batter into the prepared tin. Arrange the halved figs cut-side up on top of the batter, pressing each one down gently so it is level with the batter surface but not submerged.

Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the cake is set and a deep golden brown. The figs will have sunk slightly and the edges will look caramelised. A skewer inserted between the figs should come out clean.
Leave to cool in the tin for at least 30 minutes before removing. The cake is fragile while warm.

attrs.problem: Figs sinking completely into the batter
attrs.avoid: Avoid using figs that are too ripe and collapsing; they will sink through the batter as it bakes.
attrs.fix: Use figs that are ripe but still firm enough to hold their shape. Press them only to the surface level of the batter, not all the way in.

attrs.problem: Cake breaking apart when removed from the tin
attrs.avoid: Avoid removing from the tin while still warm; the almond-based crumb is very delicate until fully set.
attrs.fix: Leave in the tin for at least 30 minutes. Run a knife around the edge before unmoulding and turn out very gently.
